messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
char cmd[] = "go";
if (cmd == "stop") fire();
else if (cmd == "go") launch();

Question: What happens?
The student answered: it launches

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: `==` compares text

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: typed fast on a phone: all lowercase, a spelling mistake or two, little punctuation, 6 to 15 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["cmd and \"go\" have same letters so == sees them as same thing", "it checked if the text inside cmd matches the text go and it did", "since both are go the == is true so it runs launch", "cmd is holding go and \"go\" is also go so they compare equal", "the two words are the same text so the condition passes and it launches"]}

sentences: cmd and "go" have same letters so == sees them as same thing
it checked if the text inside cmd matches the text go and it did
since both are go the == is true so it runs launch
cmd is holding go and "go" is also go so they compare equal
the two words are the same text so the condition passes and it launches
